Hi Lorri Anne - thanks for more info. Indeed, scarcity of data is not a problem.

I'm checking in now with relevant teams including legal and product, and will get back to you as soon

If you call me at 1130 PT Friday we can have a quick chat. It may also be worth checking out this
existing infrastructure, Threat Exchange, which powers the GIFCT and StopNCII multisakeholder
initiatives.
Cheers, Miranda
From: Lorri Anne Meils <[contact omitted]>
Date: Thursday, March 17, 2022 at 12:04 PM
To: Miranda Sissons < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>
Cc: Amy Singh < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>, Christina Sheetz <[contact omitted]>, Laura
Pavlovic <[contact omitted]>, Sabeen Dhanani <[contact omitted]>, John O'Bryan
<[contact omitted]>, Johnny Walsh <[contact omitted]>, Meral Karan
<[contact omitted]>, Patricia Hunter <[contact omitted]>, Kira Mitre
<[contact omitted]>
Subject: Re: USAID and Digital Evidence in Ukraine
Hi Miranda,
Thanks so much for the quick response. We've been in conversations with organizations that process
digital evidence for purposes of verification and preservation. One organization (Berkeley Law
School, Human Rights Clinic, Investigations Lab) suggested that the quantity of potential digital
evidence has outpaced their ability to gather, organize and preserve it. They suggested a call to
action among social media platforms to collaborate/coordinate in developing a new "button" that can
be labeled "Ukraine Evidence" that could be installed at the point of photo/video upload. Once
uploaded using this button the information would be stored in a common, trusted repository and made
available to verified organizations for purposes of further categorization, verification and
preservation.
We are reaching out to multiple social media companies to gauge interest in collaborating on this
feature. We would appreciate any time you or others at Meta have to further discuss next Monday if
that would work for you.
Many thanks,
Lorri
Lorri Anne Meils
Human Rights, Technology and Authoritarianism Advisor
Center of Excellence for Democracy, Human Rights and Governance

Thanks for being in touch. Tomorrow is a company holiday. Can I get more idea of the promising

Cheers, interested in hearing more,
Miranda
Miranda Sissons
Director, Human Rights Policy
Meta

From: Lorri Anne Meils <[contact omitted]>
Sent: Thursday, March 17.2022 8:20:21 AM
To: Miranda Sissons < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>
Cc: Amy Singh < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Christina Sheetz <[contact omitted]>; Laura Pavlovic
<[contact omitted]>; Sabeen Dhanani <[contact omitted]>; John O'Bryan
<[contact omitted]>; Johnny Walsh <[contact omitted]>; Meral Karan <[contact omitted]>;
Patricia Hunter <[contact omitted]>; Kira Mitre <[contact omitted]>
Subject: USAID and Digital Evidence in Ukraine
Hi Miranda,
I hope this email finds you well. You may recall we were in touch last year regarding USAID's
digital democracy work and the Summit for Democracy.
I am reaching out today on a different but related workstream. USAID is exploring a promising
recommendation in connection with the preservation and verification of digital evidence in Ukraine
and we are hoping to discuss this with you and others at Meta that work on human rights issues.

Would you be available tomorrow morning at 11:30AM Pacific time for a 30 minute call? We could
also make 12or 12:30 work if those are more convenient for you. Many thanks in advance for
taking the time and we very much look forward to connecting.
Best,
Lorri
Lorri Anne Meils
